The population of Lagos is notoriously difficult to measure precisely due to rapid urbanization, high informal settlement rates, and the large lag between reliable census data (the last nationwide census was in 2006). However, based on the United Nations World Urbanization Prospects and demographic projections from the World Bank and National Bureau of Statistics for 2023–2024, the urban agglomeration (metropolitan area) is the standard metric used for international comparisons.

While the 2006 census estimated the population at roughly 8 million, growth rates for Lagos have historically been among the highest globally (often estimated between 3% and 4% annually). UN projections for the Lagos urban agglomeration place the population at approximately 16.1 million in 2020 and 18.0 million by 2025. Interpolating for the current year (2024), a figure of 17,000,000 represents the most accurate consensus point estimate among credible international demographic bodies for the metropolitan area.
